doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York clubs and the Embers trio
title: A six-week gig and the George Wein concert in Boston
summary: The Hawkins and Eldridge engagement lasted about six weeks; George Wein flew them to Boston for a Sunday concert, issued on Savoy with a poor piano and Nat Hentoff introducing her as Marian Page McPartland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That would have been interesting. Also, how long did they . . . you played on that engagement for ten years, but how long did they, Coleman Hawkins and Roy Eldridge, stay?

No, this was just about a six-weeks gig. This was at the Embers, not the Hickory House. It was pre-Hickory House. But we did some other things. George Wein was just starting in Boston. He flew us up to do a Sunday afternoon concert. Savoy did record that. I’m sorry they did, because the piano was awful. I was listening to that in Chicago. Jimmy’s granddaughter had that on a CD she brought with her from France for me to hear. I didn’t want to hear this thing. They shouldn’t even put out this old stuff. Nat Hentoff was the m.c. He’s introducing me as Marian Page McPartland. The first and last time I’ve ever heard that one.
